images.title: Keep the share equal
images.purpose: Set up the first sharing: 5 glasses for 4 friends, then twice as many friends, so the child multiplies both numbers by the same number to find the missing glasses.
images.composition: Two sharing rows stacked with a wide gap, a curved arrow on the right linking the friends numbers, and one cue line below.
images.exact_structure: Top row: 5 plain glasses of juice of the same size in a line, outlined teal #0072B2, with its caption to the right. Bottom row: one empty amber #E69F00 outlined box with a question mark in place of glasses, with its caption to the right. One reddish purple #CC79A7 curved arrow on the far right goes from the top caption to the bottom caption, labelled with the multiplier. Cue line centred at the bottom. Exactly 5 glasses, 1 empty box, 1 arrow.
labels: multiply both by the same number
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
the numbers 10, 9 or 14 anywhere, any glasses drawn in the bottom row, or the fraction 10/8
images.takeaway: To keep each share the same, multiply both numbers of the sharing by the same number.
images.description: Five glasses for 4 friends above a ? box for 8 friends, an arrow marked × 2 between the friends numbers, and the cue multiply both by the same number.
images.context: Shown with the concept as its one key picture, next to the walkthrough video. PLACEHOLDER: specified, not generated yet.
images.teaching_notes: Ask the student to say what the friends were multiplied by, and what the glasses must be multiplied by too.

image_decisions.why: A picture of one sharing and its doubled version shows the multiply idea that the missing numbers need, without the answers.
